GasSettings.cheap_tooltip: Gas values will be set to minimize the fee you pay. The transaction may stay pending longer before it confirms.
GasSettings.fast_tooltip: Gas values will be set to minimize the time your transaction takes to confirm. This may result in a higher gas fee.
GasSettings.custom_tooltip: With custom transaction configuration you can set the gas values manually.
GasSettings.eip1559_tooltip: There are two types of transactions: EIP-1559 and legacy. The type affects the formula used to calculate gas payments. EIP-1559 transactions are recommended for networks and wallets that support them.
GasSettings.legacy_tooltip: There are two types of transactions: EIP-1559 and legacy. The type affects the formula used to calculate gas payments. Legacy transactions let you set the exact gasPrice you pay. EIP-1559 transactions are recommended for networks that support them.
GasSettings.max_fee_tooltip: The fee you pay is calculated as (baseFee + priorityFee) * gasUsed. The base fee depends on network load. The priority fee is set by the sender. The gas used depends on what your transaction does. Max fee sets the upper limit on what your transaction can cost in total. The transaction will not confirm until the network base fee is low enough to stay within the max fee.
GasSettings.priority_fee_tooltip: The fee you pay is calculated as (baseFee + priorityFee) * gasUsed. A higher priority fee can get your transaction confirmed sooner, as long as the total stays within the max fee.
GasSettings.gas_limit_tooltip: The fee you pay is calculated as (baseFee + priorityFee) * gasUsed. The gas limit sets the upper bound for gasUsed in this formula. If your transaction uses less gas than the limit, you only pay for the gas it uses and the rest is refunded. Setting a low gas limit may make the transaction fail if the actions it triggers need more gas than the limit.
GasSettings.gas_price_tooltip: With a legacy transaction, the fee you pay is calculated as gasPrice * gasUsed. Your transaction will not confirm until your gasPrice is higher than or equal to the network gas price in the latest block.
GasSettings.title: Gas settings
GasSettings.priority_fee_hint: Changing the priority fee only makes the transaction cheaper or speeds it up at the cost of a higher fee.

GasSettings.priority_fee_too_high: Max priority fee per gas is unnecessarily high for current network conditions
GasSettings.gas_price_too_low: Gas price is too low for current network conditions
GasSettings.gas_price_too_high: Gas price is unnecessarily high for current network conditions
GasSettings.gas_limit_too_low: Gas limit is lower than recommended

Swap.tokens_in_two_standards_title: Tokens in ERC-20 and ERC-223 standards
Swap.tokens_in_two_standards_paragraph: Since July 27, 2023, all the tokens on Ethereum mainnet are available in two "versions": ERC-20 and ERC-223. You can always convert one version of the token to another at a 1:1 rate on DEX223 or through the <convert>converter</convert>. ERC-223 tokens may require less gas to be swapped for another token. Most centralized exchanges do not support ERC-223 deposits yet.
Swap.why_do_i_have_to_approve: Why do I have to approve a token?
Swap.confirm_action_in_your_wallet_alert: Please confirm action in your wallet
Swap.swap_is_unavailable_for_this_pair: Swap is unavailable for this pair
Swap.erc20_tooltip: ERC-20 is a token standard on Ethereum network. It specifies the "version" of the token you are going to use.
Swap.erc223_tooltip: ERC-223 is an alternative token standard on Ethereum network. It specifies the "version" of the token you are going to use. ERC-223 introduces security improvements and gas optimizations not available with ERC-20.
Swap.network_fee_tooltip: A network fee is charged for every transaction you send on the {networkName} network. It is paid in the network's native currency (for example, ETH on Ethereum).
Swap.minimum_received_tooltip: The minimum amount of tokens you will receive when the swap executes. The final price can differ from the quote, because prices come from the current block while your transaction can only confirm in a later one. You will never receive less than this amount, even if the price changes while the transaction is pending.
Swap.price_impact_tooltip: Estimated impact of your trade on the market. When you buy or sell an asset, its price moves as a result. This shows how much of that move your trade causes.
Swap.trading_fee_tooltip: Each swap pays a pool trading fee to liquidity providers. A separate protocol fee share can be collected into the Revenue contract for users who stake the staking token there.
Swap.route_tooltip: If your trade has a large impact on the market, you may get a better price by splitting it across several pools instead of trading the whole amount in one pool. Route shows the other token pairs your trade goes through, if any.
Swap.maximum_slippage_tooltip: The final swap price can differ from the price when you send the transaction. Slippage sets how much price change you accept. If the actual price differs from the expected price by more than the maximum slippage, the transaction reverts automatically and your tokens are not swapped.
Swap.gas_limit_tooltip: The gas limit sets how much work your transaction can do. The more complex the actions your transaction triggers in the smart contract, the higher the gas limit it may need. A higher gas limit can mean a higher network fee.
Swap.deadline_tooltip: The transaction deadline sets how long your queued transaction stays valid. A transaction can stay pending for a long time if gas values are low or the network is busy. If it confirms after the deadline, it reverts automatically (you pay for gas but no swap happens).
Swap.slippage_tooltip: The final swap price can differ from the price when you send the transaction. Slippage sets how much price change you accept. For example, with 5% slippage, if the pool price moves more than 5% from the expected price, your transaction fails automatically (you pay for gas but no swap happens).
Swap.approve_amount_tooltip: To swap an ERC-20 token, give the DEX contract permission to withdraw your tokens. Every DEX requires this. You set how many tokens the contract may transfer for you. This amount does not expire.
Swap.slippage_above_one: Slippage tolerance above 1% could result in an unfavorable exchange rate. Use the auto setting unless you know what you are doing.
Swap.slippage_low: Slippage below 0.05% may result in a failed transaction
Swap.eip7702_title: This wallet can't receive the ERC-223 version
Swap.eip7702_warning: Your wallet account is a smart account (EIP-7702), for example a MetaMask smart account. Smart accounts can hold and send ERC-223 tokens, including the ones you already have, but can't receive new ones. Nothing has been sent and your funds are safe.
Swap.eip7702_fix: <receive>Receive the ERC-20 version instead</receive>, or switch your wallet back to a standard account to receive ERC-223.
Swap.swap_no_liquidity: Swap unavailable. One of the tokens lacks liquidity. Please try again later or choose another pair.

Swap.tx_failed_gas_or_contract: Transaction failed due to lack of gas or an internal contract error. Try using higher slippage or gas to ensure your transaction is completed. If you still have issues, ask in our <discord>Discord</discord>.
Swap.tx_failed_out_of_gas: Transaction failed due to lack of gas. Try increasing the gas limit to ensure your transaction is completed. If you still have issues, contact support.
Swap.gas_price_tooltip: The network fee is calculated as gas used × gas price. If the gas price of your transaction is lower than the current network gas price, your transaction will not confirm until network gas prices drop.

Guidelines.title: Guidelines
Guidelines.description: Quick links to get started on DEX223.
Guidelines.getting_started_subtitle: Your first steps on the platform

swap.title: How to swap
swap.description: Trade tokens on DEX223 in a few steps.

before.heading: Before you start
before.body: Connect a wallet that holds the token you want to sell, and enough gas for the network you selected.

items.s2: Choose the token you pay with and the token you receive.
items.s3: Enter an amount. Review the quoted price and price impact.
items.s4: Confirm the swap in your wallet when prompted.

items.s1: Prefer liquid pools for tighter quotes.
items.s2: If a token is missing, open Manage tokens in the token picker or paste its contract address.
items.s3: ERC-20 and ERC-223 versions of the same asset may both appear. Pick the standard your wallet and destination expect.

converter.title: Convert ERC-20 and ERC-223
converter.description: Move any supported token between standards at a 1:1 rate.

what.heading: What it does
what.body: The converter wraps or unwraps a token between ERC-20 and ERC-223 at a 1:1 rate with no protocol fee.

items.s1: Open Token converter from the More menu.
items.s2: Select the token and the direction (to ERC-20 or to ERC-223).
items.s3: Enter the amount and confirm in your wallet.

items.s1: You received ERC-223 but a dapp only accepts ERC-20 (or the reverse).
items.s2: You are preparing liquidity or a swap that expects a specific standard.

token-lists.title: Manage token lists
token-lists.description: Enable, import, and organize the lists that power the token picker.

why.heading: Why lists matter
why.body: DEX223 only shows tokens from lists you enable. If a token is missing in Swap or Convert, check your lists first.

items.s1: Open Token lists from the More menu, or Manage tokens in the token picker.
items.s2: On the Lists tab, enable the lists you trust.
items.s3: Import a custom list by URL, JSON, or contract when needed.
items.s4: On the Tokens tab, pin favorites or import a single token by address.

safety.heading: Safety
safety.body: Only enable lists from sources you trust. Malicious lists can surface scam tokens with familiar names.

token-listing.title: List a token
token-listing.description: Submit a token to an autolisting contract so it can trade on DEX223.

overview.heading: Overview
overview.body: Token listing registers your token with a DEX223 autolisting contract so pools and the UI can discover it.

before.heading: Before you start
before.body: The listing contract needs an existing pool. Create a pool for your token and its paired token on Pools, and add liquidity so traders can get a quote.

items.s1: Open Token listing from the main navigation.
items.s2: Choose the listing contract, your token, and the Paired token.
items.s3: Review fees and requirements for that list.
items.s4: Confirm the listing transaction in your wallet.

after.heading: After listing
after.body: Use Statistics to confirm the pool appears once subgraph indexing catches up.

fiat.title: Buy crypto with fiat
fiat.description: Fund your wallet through Onramp without leaving DEX223.

overview.heading: Overview
overview.body: The Fiat page uses Onramp so you can buy (or sell) supported assets with local payment methods.

items.s2: Connect the wallet that should receive funds.
items.s3: Choose buy or sell, then follow the Onramp widget.
items.s4: When the transfer settles, return to Swap or Portfolio to use your balance.

items.s1: Availability depends on your region and Onramp's supported rails.
items.s2: DEX223 swaps stay on DEX223. Use the Swap page for crypto-to-crypto trades.

Send.title: Safe Send
Send.description: Send tokens to any wallet or contract without the risk of losing them to an address that cannot receive them.
Send.pay_description: Pay a merchant. Your order id travels with the payment so the merchant can match it to your purchase.
Send.invoice_description: For merchants. Create a pay link with the amount, token and order id already filled in, then share it with your customer.
Send.testnet_note: Testnet demo on Sepolia. It uses free test tokens (HE, NE, AR), not real money.
Send.why_title: What is Safe Send and why does it exist?
Send.why_problem: The problem. Ordinary ERC-20 tokens do not check where they are going. If you send them to a contract that cannot handle them, the transfer still succeeds and the tokens are locked there forever. Millions of dollars in tokens have been lost this way.
Send.why_fix: The fix. Safe Send uses ERC-223, the token standard DEX223 is built on. The receiving contract has to accept the tokens. If it cannot, the transfer is rejected and your tokens stay in your wallet.
Send.why_erc20: Only have ERC-20? Choose ERC-20 below. You approve the exact amount (never unlimited), and the tokens are converted to ERC-223 and sent in the same step. You can also convert tokens yourself on the Converter page.
Send.why_modes: Send pays any wallet or contract. Pay pays a merchant and attaches your order id. Invoice is for merchants: it makes a pay link to share with a customer.
Send.send_hint: ERC-223 needs one signature. ERC-20 needs an exact approval first, then it is converted and sent.
Send.pay_hint: One transfer to the merchant's address. You never give an unlimited approval.
Send.invoice_hint: Copy the link and send it to your customer. It opens the Pay tab with these fields filled in.
Send.hold_classic: ERC-20 (approve exact amount, then convert and send)
Send.sepolia_only: Safe Send runs on the Sepolia testnet for now. Switch your wallet to Sepolia to use the test tokens.
Send.blocked: This address cannot receive the token safely. The transfer was blocked so funds do not get stuck.

TokenListing.title: Token listing
TokenListing.intro: Listing your token on our platform is straightforward. You can choose one of the following methods to get your token listed:
TokenListing.default_p1: You can add your token to the default DEX223 token list. This list is enabled by default in our interface, so every token in it is shown to users. Any user can disable this list in their interface to stop seeing its tokens.
TokenListing.default_p2: To add a token to the default DEX223 token list, open an issue on our GitHub. The DEX223 team will review the request and reply in that issue's comment thread.
TokenListing.autolisting_p1: You can list a token in any auto-listing contract. Users can enable or disable auto-listing contracts in their interface at any time. Your token is shown to a user if it is in at least one listing contract or token list they have enabled. Users also see how many of their enabled lists include your token, so being in several lists makes your token look more trustworthy. Listing contracts have different listing criteria: some require payment and others are free.

swap.title: Swap in either standard
swap.body: Pick ERC-20 or ERC-223 on each side of a trade. Concentrated liquidity keeps prices tight.

convert.title: Convert 1:1, no fees
convert.body: Move any token between ERC-20 and ERC-223 at a fixed rate with zero protocol fees.

earn.title: Earn on your liquidity
earn.body: Choose a fee tier and price range and collect fees from every trade.

margin.title: Margin from real lenders
margin.body: Borrow from on-chain lending orders with custom leverage, interest and terms.

list.title: List any token, permissionlessly
list.body: Auto-listing contracts make your token tradable as soon as it has a pool.

launch.title: Launch a token in minutes
launch.body: Create an ERC-223 token, add an ERC-20 version, then pool and list it.

why.title: Millions of dollars in ERC-20 tokens are stuck in contracts that could not receive them.
why.body: ERC-223 asks the receiver first and reverts if it cannot accept the tokens. DEX223 is built around that safety, and still trades every ERC-20.

what.a: A decentralized exchange where you can swap, provide liquidity, lend, borrow and trade on margin with ERC-20 and ERC-223 tokens.

need_erc223.q: Do I need ERC-223 tokens to use it?
need_erc223.a: No. Every pool accepts both standards. You choose ERC-20 or ERC-223 for each side of a trade, and the built-in converter moves tokens between the two at 1:1.

list.q: How do I list my token?
list.a: Open Token listing, pick an auto-listing contract and confirm. Listing is permissionless: no application or approval from the team is needed.

custodial.a: No. You trade from your own wallet and sign every transaction yourself. DEX223 never holds your keys.

fees.a: Traders pay the pool's fee tier, which goes to its liquidity providers, plus network gas. Converting between ERC-20 and ERC-223 has no protocol fee.

final.title: Start trading in under a minute
final.body: Connect a wallet, pick a pair, swap. No sign-up.

Demo.banner_text: Balances are pretend. Nothing is signed or sent to a blockchain.
Demo.title: Interactive demo
Demo.description: Practice the main DEX223 actions with pretend tokens. No wallet, no gas, no risk.
Demo.ready_text: Connect a wallet and use the same screens on Ethereum. Want practice tokens first? Use the Sepolia test app.
Demo.simulated: Simulated screen. Same layout as the live page, pretend data.
Demo.wrong_click: Click the highlighted control to continue.
Demo.insufficient_alert: You only have {balance} demo {symbol}. Lower the amount or click Max.
Demo.too_high_body: Your demo wallet has {balance} {symbol}. Enter {balance} or less to continue.
Demo.wallet_dialog_text: The demo never connects to a real wallet. Exit the demo to connect yours and use the live app.

swap.title: Swap: ERC-20 vs ERC-223
swap.description: See why ERC-20 needs an approval and ERC-223 does not.
swap.complete_text: You saw the difference: ERC-20 took an approval and a swap, ERC-223 took one transaction.

choose.title: Pick how you pay
choose.body: Every token on DEX223 has an ERC-20 and an ERC-223 version. Start with the one most wallets hold today: click the highlighted ERC-20 card.
choose.tip: You choose the standard separately for the token you pay and the token you receive.

approve.title: Approve, then swap
approve.body: ERC-20 tokens need two transactions: first you allow the exchange to spend your USDT, then you swap. Click the highlighted Approve button.
approve.tip: With ERC-223 there is no approval step, so the same swap is one transaction.

swap.title: Now the swap itself
swap.body: The approval is done. The second transaction moves your USDT into the pool and sends D223 back. Click Swap.
swap.tip: An approval left open can be abused by a malicious contract later. ERC-223 never creates one.

compare.title: Same trade, one transaction
compare.body: Paying with the ERC-223 version of USDT skips the approval. The tokens move straight into the pool in a single transaction.
compare.tip: Every pool accepts both standards. You choose ERC-20 or ERC-223 on each side of a trade.

convert.title: Convert 1:1
convert.description: Turn USDT into its ERC-223 version and back, with no fees.
convert.complete_text: You moved USDT to ERC-223 and back at exactly 1:1, with no protocol fee.

pick.title: Pick the direction
pick.body: The converter works both ways. Click the highlighted direction to turn ERC-20 USDT into ERC-223 USDT.
pick.tip: Your demo wallet already holds both versions of USDT.

convert.title: Convert to ERC-223
convert.body: The converter swaps a token between its ERC-20 and ERC-223 versions at exactly 1:1. There is no protocol fee. Click Convert.
convert.tip: You need the ERC-223 version to skip approvals when you trade.

back.title: And back again
back.body: You can always return to ERC-20, for example to send tokens to an exchange that only supports ERC-20. Click Convert back.
back.tip: Both versions are the same token. Only the way it moves is different.

liquidity.title: Add liquidity
liquidity.description: Pick a fee tier and price range, deposit two tokens, earn fees.
liquidity.complete_text: You opened a USDT / D223 position. In the live app it earns 0.3% of every trade that uses your price range.

pair.title: Pick a pair
pair.body: A position holds two tokens. This demo uses USDT and D223, already selected for you. Click Next.
pair.tip: You can deposit either standard of each token. The pool accepts both.

fee.title: Pick a fee tier
fee.body: Every trade in this pool pays its fee to liquidity providers. 0.3% suits most pairs. Click the highlighted tier.
fee.tip: Lower tiers suit stable pairs; higher tiers suit volatile tokens.

range.title: Set a price range
range.body: Your liquidity only earns fees while the price is inside your range. Click Use suggested range to fill in a range around the current price.
range.tip: A narrow range earns more per trade but goes out of range more often.

deposit.title: Check the amounts
deposit.body: The app works out how much of each token the range needs. Here it is 100 USDT and 12,431.2 D223. Click Next.
deposit.tip: Amounts are pretend. In the live app you can deposit any amount up to your balance.

add.title: Add the position
add.body: One last check, then the position is created. Click Add liquidity.
add.tip: Collected fees can be claimed from Pools at any time.

listing.title: List a token and trade on margin
listing.description: List a token with an auto-listing contract, then borrow from a lending order.
listing.complete_text: You listed a token without asking anyone and opened a margin position from an on-chain lending order.

token.title: Pick a token to list
token.body: Listing is permissionless: anyone can list a token that has a pool. This demo lists a token called DEMO. Click Next.
token.tip: No application and no approval from the DEX223 team are needed.

contract.title: Choose an auto-listing contract
contract.body: Auto-listing contracts are token lists that live on chain. Some are free, some charge a fee set by their owner. Click the free one.
contract.tip: Wallets and apps can read these lists straight from the contract.

list.title: List DEMO
list.body: Listing is one transaction. Click List DEMO.
list.tip: Once listed, the token shows up in the token search for everyone using that list.

order.title: Find a lending order
order.body: Margin trading on DEX223 uses lending orders posted by other users. Each order sets its own interest, leverage and term. Click order #12.
order.tip: Lenders choose which tokens you may trade with their money.

open.title: Borrow from a lending order
open.body: You borrow against your collateral and trade inside the position. Click Open position.
open.tip: Your borrowed funds stay inside the position contract, so they can only be traded on DEX223.

watch.title: Watch the position
watch.body: The position is open. Its value, interest and liquidation price update with the market. Click Finish when you are done.
watch.tip: If the collateral value drops below the liquidation price, the position is closed automatically.
